inputs.share_count_basis: 9,972m shares in issue net of treasury at 31 March 2026 (Metrics.csv). Diluted weighted-average for FY26 was 9,939m (AR FY2026 note 10, line 10329); the period-end figure is the higher of the two and is used. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and BT's own-share purchases (£126m FY26) net of option-exercise proceeds (£96m) are what keep the count flat in practice.
inputs.net_debt_basis: BT-defined net financial debt at 31 March 2026 (AR FY2026 p.199): loans and other borrowings 18,536 less cash 359 and current asset investments 1,482, less swap retranslation 444, EIR/fair-value adjustments 240, JV loans 10, copper forward-sale loans 177, contract-asset sale loans 42 = 15,782. Lease liabilities (4,184) EXCLUDED because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). BT's headline 'net debt' of 19,966 includes leases.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was £146m (interest received £96m) but sits in investing, not in OCF, so it is not inside reported_fcf and is not deducted. BT is a net-debt company; the £1.84bn of cash and investments is netted inside net_debt, and the component build starts from operating EBITDA so no interest income enters the forward flows.
inputs.sbc_source: AR FY2026 note 22 / employee costs: share-based payment expense £49m (FY25: £62m), line 9876; equals the SOCE credit at line 9039. Tax credit on SBC £25m not added (would double count).
inputs.buyback_note: £126m 'repurchase of ordinary share capital' in financing is the purchase of own shares to satisfy employee share plans, not a value-returning buyback. BT has not run a capital-return buyback since FY2018. New policy from FY27: low-to-mid single-digit dividend growth until BBB+-consistent leverage, then enhanced distributions.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 is a unit conversion (GBP per share x 100 = pence), not an exchange rate, so no date/parity check applies. The ADR was delisted from the NYSE in 2019; no dual-listing parity available.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows. 10y gilt ~4.6%, UK ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~9.1%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (recent BT sterling/euro bonds swapped), 25% UK corporation tax -> ~4.0% after tax. Weights: market cap ~GBP19.2bn (192.75p x 9,972m) vs net financial debt GBP15.8bn -> ~55/45. WACC = 0.55 x 9.1 + 0.45 x 4.0 = 6.8%, rounded to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, regulatory and leverage risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full IFRS 16 lease payment -- principal GBP731m (financing, 'Payment of lease liabilities') + interest GBP133m (operating) = GBP864m, 4.4% of FY26 revenue -- is deducted inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (GBP4,184m) are therefore excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path uses D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: 4,875 before specific items - 610 ROU depreciation = 4,265 = 21.7% of revenue. Lease book is running down (6.5bn FY20 -> 4.2bn FY26) so the lease % glides from 4.4 to 4.0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests GBP5m at 31 March 2026 -- immaterial, no adjustment.
inputs.pension_treatment: Pension deficit repair is NOT in adjusted EBITDA, so it is charged once in the equity bridge: IAS 19 deficit GBP4.2bn gross, GBP3.1bn net of deferred tax at 31 March 2026 (AR FY2026 line 2932). Scheduled cash: GBP780m/yr FY27-FY30 (600 BT plc + 180 ABF), GBP670m FY31, GBP180m/yr FY32-FY34 (note 20, line 11925) -- PV after 25% tax relief ~GBP2.7bn at 7%, so the GBP3.1bn IAS 19 figure is the more conservative of the two and covers the risk that the June 2026 triennial extends the plan. Reported FCF (1,861) is AFTER GBP790m of deficit payments; the component forward build is BEFORE them.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US, leveraged, lease-heavy; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Not a REIT/bank/holdco. EBITDA BASIS: driver margins are BT's adjusted EBITDA margin (FY26 8,230 / 19,654 = 41.9%) LESS a recurring allowance for 'specific items' (restructuring/transformation cash, GBP415m FY26, GBP498m FY25; GBP1.4bn total cost-to-achieve for the GBP3.7bn programme to FY30), glided from 1.6% of revenue in FY27 to 0.5% in the terminal years. Reported EBITDA in Metrics.csv (7,810) already carries these items. CAPEX: guidance is ex-spectrum (~GBP4.3bn FY27, >GBP1bn below FY26's 5.1bn by FY30); the paths add ~GBP150m/yr for spectrum/other licences. TAX: cash tax paid is tiny (GBP58m FY26) because interest and pension deficit payments are deductible and capex enjoys full expensing; those two shields are charged elsewhere (WACC, bridge), so the UNLEVERED cash rate on EBIT is ~18-20% today and ramps to the 25% statutory rate by year 5 as capex falls toward D&A. INTERNATIONAL/VERIZON JV: International (~11% of revenue, low margin) stays in the consolidated paths because FY27 guidance includes it; its 2027 deconsolidation into the 50/50 JV is treated as a value-neutral swap of consolidated EBITDA for an equity-accounted stake, with the $625m (~GBP465m) equalisation payment added in the bridge. Unmodelled: residual TNT Sports JV minimum-guarantee settlements (GBP191m FY26, GBP187m FY25, running off; <~4p/share). Owner FY27 unlevered FCF (~GBP2.0bn base) reconciles to BT's ~GBP2.0bn NFCF guidance once the GBP0.9bn net interest, GBP0.15bn spectrum, GBP0.3bn specific-items allowance and unlevered tax are bridged. Base case lands ~20% below management's GBP3bn FY30 NFCF target; the bull case is the management case delivered.

equity_bridge.item: IAS 19 pension deficit, net of deferred tax (31 Mar 2026)
equity_bridge.note: AR FY2026 line 2932: GBP4.2bn gross, GBP3.1bn net. Deficit payments GBP780m/yr to FY30 are outside adjusted EBITDA, so charged here once.
Announced June 2026, completion expected 2027; converted at ~1.34 USD/GBP. International's consolidated EBITDA leaves the flows in exchange for the 50/50 stake, treated as value-neutral.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case terminal / mid-term revenue growth, anchored to FY27 guidance (GBP19.0-19.5bn) and the 'sustained growth from FY27' mid-term outlook; equity CAGR rejected as a growth source because BT's book value is dominated by IAS 19 remeasurements, not retained earnings
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-4.7% 3yr / +1.5% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (-17.0% / -5.9%) and from owner-FCF (+10.7% / +12.9%). Equity moves are pension remeasurement noise; EPS is depressed by specific items and impairments (FY24 reported NI GBP855m); owner-FCF CAGRs are flattered by a low FY21/FY23 base and pre-interest OCF. None of the three is a usable forward growth rate for a mature regulated telecom; guidance is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex, pre-interest) less SBC; the owner CAGR sits ABOVE the reported CAGR because SBC fell from GBP72m (FY21) to GBP49m (FY26). Revenue CAGRs use FY2021-FY2026 to stay clear of the Jan-2016 EE step-up (FY16 19.0bn -> FY17 24.1bn); the decline since then is divestments plus legacy voice/copper. FY0 figures are BT's 'Total (reported)' basis, not 'before specific items'.

base.narrative: FY27 revenue at the mid-low end of the GBP19.0-19.5bn guide (voice headwind, International decline), stabilising from FY29 and growing ~1% thereafter with FTTP ARPU offsetting line losses. Adjusted EBITDA margin 43.0% in FY27 (GBP8.24bn, inside the 8.2-8.3bn guide) rising to 45.5% by FY31 as the GBP3.7bn cost programme lands, less a specific-items allowance gliding 1.6% -> 0.5%. Capex GBP4.45bn FY27 incl. spectrum, falling to ~GBP4.1bn FY30 and ~20% of revenue (capex/D&A ~1.05) in the terminal years. Unlevered cash tax 18% -> 25% by FY31. Terminal cap 14x unlevered owner FCF binds over Gordon at 7%/1%.

bull.narrative: The management case delivered: 'sustained growth from FY27' materialises as ~2% revenue growth FY30-FY32 on FTTP take-up and CPI-linked wholesale pricing, EBITDA grows ahead of revenue to a 47% margin, capex ex-spectrum drops below GBP4bn by FY30 and the FY30 NFCF reaches ~GBP3bn. Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 15x.

bear.narrative: Altnet overbuild (CityFibre, Nexfibre+Netomnia) and VMO2 keep Openreach losing 700k+ lines a year, Ofcom's TAR 2026-31 caps the ARPU response, Vodafone-Three pressures EE pricing, and revenue keeps shrinking 1-3.5% a year before flattening at ~GBP17bn. Cost savings are absorbed by wage/NI inflation so the net margin stays ~41.5%; capex stays elevated (~21.5-24% of revenue) to defend the footprint. Zero terminal growth, 12x cap. With GBP15.8bn of net financial debt and a GBP3.1bn pension deficit ahead of equity, the leverage magnifies the hit.

scenario_narratives.base: Capex rolls off as guided (GBP5.1bn -> ~GBP4.3bn FY27 -> ~GBP4.0bn FY30 ex-spectrum) and most of the GBP3.7bn cost programme is delivered, lifting the adjusted EBITDA margin from 42% to ~45% while revenue bottoms in FY28 and grows ~1% thereafter. Unlevered owner FCF rises from ~GBP2.0bn to ~GBP3.1bn by FY36; the valuation sits ~20% below management's GBP3bn FY30 NFCF because spectrum, recurring restructuring cash and a normalising 25% unlevered tax rate are charged. Pension deficit (GBP3.1bn net) and GBP15.8bn net financial debt are deducted once in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's plan lands in full: FTTP take-up and CPI-linked wholesale pricing give sustained ~2% revenue growth, margins reach 47%, capex falls below GBP4bn and NFCF hits ~GBP3bn in FY30; the balance sheet reaches BBB+ metrics and enhanced distributions begin, supporting a 15x terminal multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Infrastructure competition and Ofcom cap Openreach's monetisation of the fibre build, revenue erodes toward GBP17bn, the cost programme only offsets inflation, and capex has to stay high to defend footprint. Leverage and the pension deficit absorb most of the enterprise value and the equity is worth less than half today's price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: ~4.5x net-debt-plus-pension to EBITDA leverage makes the equity a thin slice of EV, the core asset's returns depend on a single regulator (Ofcom) that has already intervened against Openreach pricing in this review period, Openreach is still losing 800k+ lines a year to overbuild, and the CFO, Openreach CEO and several ExCo roles changed hands during the inflection. Bull cut to 25%: it needs capex, cost delivery, revenue stabilisation AND a benign tax/regulatory path to all go right simultaneously; the 'cash-flow inflection' thesis is also already partly in the price after the re-rating to a 7-year high.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BT is valued as an unlevered stream of owner FCF -- adjusted EBITDA less recurring restructuring cash, SBC, the full IFRS 16 lease payment, unlevered cash tax at a rate ramping to statutory, and capex including spectrum -- discounted at a sterling 7% WACC, with net financial debt, the after-tax IAS 19 pension deficit and the Verizon equalisation receipt bridged once. The thesis the market is paying for is the capex-peak-to-cash inflection; the base case gives management most but not all of it, and the equity's sensitivity to that delivery is what the bear/bull spread shows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: GBP15.8bn net financial debt plus a GBP3.1bn after-tax pension deficit sit ahead of GBP19bn of equity -- a 10% move in EV is roughly a 20% move in the shares
Capex roll-off slips (30m-premises extension, spectrum auctions, overbuild defence) and the FCF inflection arrives later or smaller than guided
Ofcom Telecoms Access Review 2026-31 and future reviews cap Openreach wholesale pricing below what FTTP take-up would otherwise deliver
Altnet/VMO2/Nexfibre overbuild accelerates Openreach line losses beyond the ~800k/yr run-rate
Cash tax normalises faster than the 5-year ramp assumed as full-expensing capex falls and interest/pension shields shrink
June 2026 triennial pension valuation extends or increases deficit repair beyond the current FY31 end-date
Governance: Bharti Global's 24.5% stake and two board seats; concurrent CFO/Openreach CEO/ExCo turnover during the transition
